207.author: zhaozhaozz
207.body:
The Nightly on `dec6c686` ([run 36188684291](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/36188684291)) failed one journey: `journey-compact-process.spec.ts:138`, the check that a completed `run_shell` record has no border, expected `borderTopWidth` `"0px"` and received `""`. The same commit passed on the push CI ([35979748259](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/35979748259)) and on the previous Nightly ([36058461332](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/36058461332)), and `main` has not moved since, so this is a race in the test rather than a change in the product.

`""` is not a thin border. It is what Chromium returns for every computed style property of an element that is no longer in the document. The test read the card at the moment the page was replacing it.

## Root cause

Two things combine.

**A finished run's cards are mounted afresh.** A run is streamed into the live timeline, which `App` renders after the conversation blocks. Once it ends, the session refresh replays its persisted events and it is rendered inside the blocks, under `Fragment key="run-<id>"`. Those are different subtrees, so React mounts every card in the record and removes the live ones. A `MutationObserver` on the journey records exactly one removal of the completed `run_shell` record around completion, every run, and the removed node already carries `completed process-record` — exactly what the test's locator matches.

**`locator.evaluate` is two round trips.** In the pinned Playwright 1.61.1 it is `waitForSelector` to resolve an `ElementHandle`, then the function runs against that handle. The page keeps running in between.

Whether the hand-off lands before or after the API reports the run terminal varies. Locally it landed 500 ms before `waitForRunTerminal` returned, so the test only ever saw the record. The Nightly's trace shows the other order:

| UTC | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 20:58:46.508 | `toHaveClass(/process-record/)` starts, passes |
| 20:58:46.534 | page requests `GET /runs/<id>/events` — the replay that builds the record |
| 20:58:46.556 | `waitForSelector` resolves the handle to `<details class="timeline-disclosure tool completed process-record">` |
| 20:58:46.619 | failure screenshot; the handle's `getComputedStyle` read `""` in between |

Holding that replay in the browser and releasing it between the two steps `locator.evaluate` performs reproduces the Nightly's value on every run: `{"connected":false,"borderTopWidth":""}`.

## The fix

Replacing the `evaluate` with `toHaveCSS` alone is not enough. A web-first assertion queries and reads in a single evaluation, so it cannot see a detached node — but it would pass at once on the live card, which is also `0px`, and move the race onto the one-shot `boundingBox()` reads a few lines further down, which land right in the hand-off window by the Nightly's own timings.

The step has to measure the record, and nothing in the DOM told the two apart: the same `<section class="run-timeline">`, the same header, the same parent. So `RunTimeline` takes an optional `recordedRunId`, rendered as `data-run-record`, and `App` passes it for the record only. The step looks the card up inside `.run-timeline[data-run-record="<runId>"]`; its assertions wait for the record to exist, and every read after them is on a node that is not replaced again.

The `0px` check becomes `toHaveCSS("border-top-width", "0px")`, and so does the re-collapse check one step later, which is the same one-shot read of the same record. The expectation is unchanged.

The attribute is omitted when the prop is not passed, so the live timeline and the sub-agent conversation render exactly as before.

## Validation

Tested SHA: `ea392f7a8f607d9066ac69f0153eb0f635f8bdba`.

| Layer | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UT | `pnpm ci:ut` | PASS — 3170 planned / 3170 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped |
| ST | `pnpm ci:st` | PASS — 1/1 |
| E2E | `.ci/run-e2e.sh mocked` with `E2E_SCIENTIFIC_ENVS=1`, as the tagged runner invokes it | 44 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped (the existing `test.fixme` in `literature-review`); `check-e2e-meta` 48 spec files, 0 errors |

The five web test files that render `RunTimeline` (`RunTimeline`, `SessionRunTimelines`, `ProcessLifecycle`, `RunStopFlow`, `UiUsability`): 100/100.

## E2E user journeys

The journey this changes, `test/journey-compact-process.spec.ts:43`, run against an isolated stack started the way the E2E layer starts it:

| Scenario | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Natural timing, `--repeat-each=5` | every run passes | PASS 5/5 |
| Replay held 3 s, so the record mounts after the API reports terminal — the Nightly's order | record absent when the API says terminal; step waits for it and passes | PASS 3/3; record count at terminal was 0 in all three |
| Replay released between resolving the card and reading it, as `locator.evaluate` does | old read returns `""`; the fixed assertions pass in that same state | old read `{"connected":false,"borderTopWidth":""}` 3/3; fixed step PASS 3/3 |

The last two scenarios used temporary copies of the spec with a route holding the replay request; they are not part of this change.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`

User impact: none. The timeline renders identically; a finished run's record now carries a `data-run-record` attribute naming its run.

Compatibility and migration: none.

212.author: Birfy
212.body:
Fixes #210. This PR targets `feat/jiuwenswarm` and supersedes #211. The local memory graph now computes folded products by visiting each scope child once, so branching `next` paths cannot multiply the folded view's intermediate rows. It preserves the child identity used by surrogate edges and group expansion.

## Review follow-up from #211

- Share relationship-path prefixes with a compact immutable reference and a depth-first active-edge set. The interpreter materializes a relationship list only when the query reads that path; ordinary long-chain counts now succeed in linear memory. A payload budget still protects requests that actually return many full paths.
- Apply the same work, time, row, and collection budget to top-level and nested clauses, including `CALL`, `FOREACH`, `UNWIND`, `CREATE`, fixed-length expansion, aggregation, and writes. The statement rolls back on a budget error. This bounds the covered interpreter operations; it is not a process-level memory isolation guarantee.
- Put session and scope predicates inside node patterns for subgraph, scope expansion, and group expansion reads. The local property index now narrows candidates before charging query work, so unrelated historical nodes do not make a fresh session fail.
- Preserve `CypherBudgetExceeded` through write-route handlers so read and write endpoints return the same structured HTTP 503 (`memory_graph_query_limit`).
- Rebuild scope and temporal `next` edges by method, and keep subagent children out of the main temporal chain.
- Evaluate row-independent projection expressions once and reuse exported collection values across result rows. This lets the review query return all 4,000 rows while allocating only one copy of its repeated 4,000-element list. A cumulative per-statement element budget still guards genuinely distinct large collections before allocation, including `range()`, list concatenation, literals, slices, `collect()`, and result export; query logs include `collection_elements`.

## Reachability and follow-up to the new review comment

The HTTP service exposes fixed query endpoints, not a raw Cypher endpoint. Its internal local backend still executes production statements using `collect()`, `range()`, and list concatenation, with lengths that can depend on stored data. I included cumulative accounting in this PR because those existing statements can reach the same allocation mechanisms. The limit covers interpreter-created collection slots; it is not a universal process-memory cap or a bound on graph storage and arbitrary scalar strings.

On the reviewer's exact `UNWIND range(1, 4000) AS i RETURN range(1, 4000) AS xs` query, the previous `afc5d900` code was killed by a **128,000 KiB polling RSS watchdog** (observed **138,528 KiB**, no result, **95 ms total process time**) on the same macOS host. The updated `b11b77a1` code returns **4,000 rows × 4,000 values in 5.6 ms**, with **24,960 KiB peak RSS** and `collection_elements=12000`. A row-dependent variant (`range(i, i + 3999)`) still stops with `CypherBudgetExceeded` before materializing 16 million distinct elements; the exact repeated-value scenario completes. A caller that serializes all 16 million logical output values still incurs the corresponding output cost; the service has no raw Cypher response endpoint. This is a separate same-host comparison from the reviewer's Linux `RLIMIT_AS` reproduction; the local watchdog is not an OS-enforced limit.

## Validation

- Local memory graph suite on `b11b77a1`: 186 passed, 1 deselected (`test_legacy_artifact_id_constraint_dropped` requires Neo4j server constraints), 0 failed. It includes real relationship-path output, cycle semantics, long-chain counting, nested write rollback, fresh-session indexing, and write-route 503 responses.
- [Linux GitHub Actions CI on `b11b77a1`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/36287493403): UT **3,684/3,684 passed**, ST **2/2 passed**, mocked E2E **69/69 passed**; Docker image, both binary releases, and coverage also passed. The real E2E job is daily-only and was skipped by design.
- Native `pnpm ci:ut` on `afc5d900`: 3,680 planned / 0 executed / 0 passed; preflight `HOST_MISMATCH` because this host is macOS/arm64 and the shared plan requires Linux/amd64. The unmodified target branch has the same preflight result (3,670 planned / 0 executed). The Linux CI run is the authoritative full layer.
- Native `pnpm ci:st`: 2 planned / 0 executed / 0 passed for the same `HOST_MISMATCH`; unmodified target branch: 2 planned / 0 executed.
- Native `pnpm ci:e2e`: 69 planned / 0 executed / 0 passed for the same `HOST_MISMATCH` after browser preparation; unmodified target branch: 69 planned / 0 executed.

### Before/after memory and query time

These are local measurements in separate child processes over in-memory synthetic graphs, with a 25-second timeout and a polling RSS watchdog. The watchdog kills after observing a threshold; it is not an OS-enforced address-space limit. Peak RSS includes Python and the graph; the delta starts immediately before the query. A terminated run has no completed query time, so the time shown for it is total child-process time to the watchdog, including graph setup.

| Scenario | Before | After on `b11b77a1` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 18 branch/rejoin diamonds, folded view | `feat/jiuwenswarm` `acc660b2`: no result; RSS passed 256,000 KiB at 1.97 s total | 57 nodes / 75 edges in **3.1 ms**; peak **32,176 KiB**, query delta **+256 KiB** |
| 7,001-node linear path, `RETURN count(b)` | old PR #211 `b39fcd9f`: no result; RSS passed 128,000 KiB at 0.83 s total | count **7,001** in **31.0 ms**; peak **47,824 KiB**, query delta **+5,472 KiB** |
| 20,001-node linear path | old PR #211's smaller 7,001-node case already exceeded 128 MiB | count **20,001** in **108.7 ms**; peak **76,544 KiB**, query delta **+15,616 KiB** |
| 40,001-node linear path | old PR #211's smaller 7,001-node case already exceeded 128 MiB | count **40,001** in **272.5 ms**; peak **119,872 KiB**, query delta **+29,648 KiB** |
| New empty session with 125,001 unrelated historical SearchNodes | old PR #211 `b39fcd9f`: budget error in **253.9 ms**; peak **149,504 KiB**, delta **+240 KiB** | empty graph in **1.4 ms**; peak **148,160 KiB**, query delta **+112 KiB** |

The implementation reuses the existing indexed graph and Python standard-library iterators and data classes. Adding another graph library would duplicate graph storage for this read path, while enumerating all distinct paths can still grow combinatorially.

## Problem and behavior

Two completed real E2E runs delivered artifacts but failed scoring because the Judge spent its entire output budget on reasoning: BiomniBench DA-13-3 repeat 3 (8,192 tokens) and the PUCT supplementary audit repeat 2 (32,768 tokens). Increasing the budget to 65,536 recovered scores of 77 and 86.25 respectively on the first attempt. This PR brings that experiment's recovery policy into the test engineering code.

- Give Biomni and the optional PUCT Judge 65,536 output tokens and up to three retries after the initial request. Reuse identical evidence/rubrics and accept the first valid score; never select the highest score.
- Retry incomplete/invalid responses and transient transport errors, but stop on permanent HTTP errors such as authentication or insufficient balance. Retain the request body without credentials, each returned response, and attempt status/usage/timing in an immutable attempts directory.
- Allow 900 seconds per request and a separate configurable 65-minute scoring stage so the parent test does not kill recovery early. Agent execution budgets and delivery assertions are unchanged.
- Add the previously external PUCT supplementary audit as an opt-in repository entry point (`E2E_PUCT_LLM_EVALUATION=1`). 222.body:
## Summary

**Draft — do not merge until the full UT/ST/browser-E2E gates and remaining integration acceptance checks below are completed.** The implementation is available for review; targeted validation passed, but full local validation is incomplete.

Extract Idea Tree from the evolve process into an independently runnable Python service and expose its research capabilities as session-scoped MCP tools. This is the service-extraction work for #101 (part of #84), establishing a separate lifecycle and state boundary before the evolve migration in #102.

The branch is based on upstream `main` at `5de0ff59eb0375f45d93a065ec701ca6573fc328`. The candidate is `8374ac7f6159a475b4743de5da276c8019b2774e` (one commit; 45 changed files, including detected moves).

## 1. Independent service and state ownership

- Move `idea_tree_service`, `research_service`, the research engine, tree models, prompts and templates from evolve's vendored implementation into `services/idea-tree/src/sciencediscovery_idea_tree`.
- Remove both router registrations from the evolve server. The new package has no imports from evolve; the existing research algorithm is preserved rather than rewritten as part of the extraction.
- Add a dedicated FastAPI entry point, health endpoint, locked dependencies, shutdown cleanup and service-only authentication. Standalone startup fails closed without `SCIENCE_AGENT_IDEA_TREE_INTERNAL_TOKEN`.
- Use a dedicated state root (`SCIENCE_AGENT_IDEA_TREE_DATA_DIR`, defaulting under the shared data root's `idea-tree` directory), atomic JSON persistence and independently persisted research settings.
- Copy legacy tree/research records on first startup without deleting originals. A migration marker prevents re-importing stale legacy data; conflicting destination records fail startup instead of overwriting data. Import the old API catalog's settings once, then keep settings authoritative in the service.
- Serve persisted skill references so skill deletion-impact checks include autonomous research as well as historical trees and chat-run references.

## 2. Service-owned MCP tools and capability isolation

The service publishes four tool contracts:

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `create_idea_research` | Start autonomous research with an objective and prepared evidence/materials |
| `get_idea_research` | Query the current session's research and findings |
| `control_idea_research` | Pause, continue or end research |
| `view_idea_tree` | Read a historical tree graph |

The trusted control plane provisions a five-minute capability using its service credential. The scoped MCP endpoint supports initialization, discovery, calls, ping, notifications and revocation. Project/session identity and model callback credentials come from that trusted scope, not model-supplied tool arguments. Continue grants are pinned to a specific research ID. Expired scopes are rejected, active scope count is bounded, and revoking a transport scope does not terminate autonomous research. Access logging is disabled for this process to avoid logging capability URLs.

The API obtains schemas from the service and contributes them to the existing JiuwenSwarm MCP bridge/native executor. The former hard-coded create/get tool definitions in `packages/evolve` are removed. Tool discovery failure does not prevent unrelated chat tools from being used.

## 3. TypeScript client and unchanged frontend interfaces

- Replace `services/api/src/idea-tree/python-client.ts` with `IdeaTreeServiceClient` in `packages/idea-tree`. The client provides authenticated, bounded HTTP transport, dynamic tool discovery, scoped MCP research calls, settings transport and historical-tree reads.
- Route active research through the independent service rather than evolve. Preserve the research-created event, create-time chat messages and SSE forwarding.
- Keep historical compatibility types/read transport in `packages/idea-tree`; legacy mutating `tree_*` tools remain disabled.
- Preserve all six frontend paths and their existing response shapes:

| Interface | Handling after this change | Contract mapping |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` | Research service command/query | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `POST /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` | Independent research lifecycle; control plane retains chat-message creation | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research/:researchId/events` | Independent service SSE, forwarded through the existing public route | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/graph` | Historical graph read from independent storage | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `GET /api/settings/idea-tree` | Service-owned settings | New `idea-tree-settings-noop` |
| `PUT /api/settings/idea-tree` | Service-owned partial update, preserving values on an empty update | New `idea-tree-settings-noop` |

These are contract-case mappings, not a claim that a full baseline/candidate L1 differential run passed. The committed lifecycle golden fixture records the stable `running → paused → paused after restart → completed` projection and is asserted by the service journey; it is not a complete chat/agent event-stream golden trace.

## 4. Startup, packaging and test discovery

- Provision/start the new service through `scripts/start-stack.sh` and include it in the Docker image.
- Default to loopback port `4314`; reserve `4414` for the isolated browser-test stack and include it in busy-port checks.
- Add `pnpm idea-tree:test`, relocate the existing Python tree/research tests with the service, and include the service in tagged test discovery, environment preparation and coverage roots.
- Add standalone-service documentation covering configuration, migration and the remaining control-plane boundary.

## Compatibility, migration and scope boundaries

- Stop the old stack before upgrading. The maintained startup script/Docker packaging includes the new process; custom process supervisors must launch it and provide matching service URL/token configuration.
- Run one ASGI worker: background research tasks and short-lived scopes are process-local. Research and settings are persisted; the journey verifies recovery of paused research after restart.
- The adapter still reaches these frontend routes through the existing API control plane. Session ownership, chat-message writes and model-secret provisioning are **not** moved into the new service by this PR.
- Research still uses the existing run-bound LLM callback pending #102; it does not receive provider API keys. Extracting the service does not remove that callback dependency from the wider stack.
- Prepared evidence is preserved, but this PR does not implement the artifact/provenance/CAS service tracked by #98 or change its ownership.
- This PR does not claim completion of the broader JiuwenSwarm migration or the full #101 integration acceptance matrix; full public-route differential and chat/agent trace verification remain review/validation follow-ups.

## Validation

Tested candidate: `8374ac7f6159a475b4743de5da276c8019b2774e`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm build` | PASS, recursive workspace build |
| `pnpm typecheck` | PASS, including test TypeScript configuration |
| Independent-service Python suite | 34 passed |
| `packages/evolve/src/index.test.ts` + `packages/idea-tree/src/client.test.ts` under Linux | 11 passed |
| `node test/contract/run.mjs --coverage` | Mapping check passed: 151/254 repository interface rows mapped; not 151 executed tests |
| `bash -n scripts/start-stack.sh` and `bash -n .ci/run-e2e.sh` | PASS |
| `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check` | PASS |

Full local gates were attempted in separate checkouts of the candidate and unmodified upstream baseline `5de0ff59`:

- **UT: BLOCKED / incomplete.** `pnpm ci:ut` remained in JiuwenSwarm dependency preparation, downloading/building its Python dependencies, before the shared test runner started. The candidate attempt was manually stopped after approximately ten minutes in this layer; the baseline attempt was also stopped while in the same preparation stage. Both wrappers then recorded exit code 2 (`JiuwenSwarm could not be installed`). This is an interrupted preparation attempt, not an observed product assertion failure, and it does not establish that UT would fail on a fully provisioned host. No frozen plan or planned/executed/passed test summary was generated; those counts are unavailable, not zero-pass success.
- **ST: incomplete, with one smoke passing.** Both checkouts built successfully. The first attempts failed before planning (`A revision is required`) because WSL Git could not resolve the Windows-created temporary worktree metadata. After repairing only that metadata, both retries froze two identities. The candidate's native agent-loop smoke group reports **planned 1 / executed 1 / passed 1 / failed 0 / skipped 0**; the baseline emitted the same smoke's pass event. The other identity, `swarm-sdk-contract`, requires JiuwenSwarm setup, which was still preparing dependencies when the run was stopped. No complete two-identity ST summary is available. The retries reused the exact SHA's completed install/build via `CI_E2E_PREPARED=1`; no test selection was removed.
- **Browser E2E: incomplete / not executed.** `pnpm ci:e2e` was invoked on both candidate and baseline; preparation reached the pinned `.e2e` dependency installation after the workspace build. The attempts were stopped during preparation. No browser plan, executed-journey count or final summary was produced. This is not a browser PASS and not evidence of a candidate-specific failure.

Remaining local verification was deliberately stopped rather than leaving background preparation jobs running. The draft status reflects these incomplete gates; a fully provisioned Linux/CI run is still required. The initial worktree metadata error was a local harness issue, not a source change; the dependency preparation attempts do not support claiming a pre-existing upstream product defect.

## E2E user journey

**PASS** — one independent-service API/CLI journey, seven numbered steps passed, zero failed/blocked/skipped. The driver launches the installed product CLI in a separate process, with an owned data directory and a local HTTP model stub; no paid model calls or external research services are used.

Command, from the repository root after installing the service:

```sh
services/idea-tree/.venv/bin/python test/api/idea-tree-service-journey.py
```

| Step | Expected and observed result |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Discover tools and save settings | Four MCP tools exposed; settings accepted by the independent process |
| 2. Start research with prepared evidence | Research enters `running`; the real engine reaches the local model callback |
| 3. Pause active research | Paused state persists; the delayed model response does not advance the paused stage |
| 4. Restart the service | Paused research and saved settings are recovered |
| 5. Read from another session | Cross-session capability cannot access the research |
| 6. Continue and consume SSE | 19 snapshots received; research completes with independently assessed candidate score 7; no model token in frames |
| 7. Check references and delete owned research | Persistent skill reference detected; owned session research removed |

This service-level journey does not substitute for the full browser stack, public API/JiuwenSwarm integration or a live-model test. Docker/release-binary execution was not locally verified.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature`

User impact: research is hosted in a dedicated service with explicit MCP lifecycle controls and persistent, independently owned settings/state. Existing frontend paths remain stable.

The contributor has read-only access to upstream (`push: false`, `triage: false`), so the GitHub `release:feature` label is **pending a maintainer**; it has not been applied.

The release branch `releases/v0.3.0.beta` should no longer get a daily build. It never had one of its own: GitHub evaluates `schedule` only on the default branch, so the cron in the release branch's `nightly.yml` does not fire. It was built daily because `main`'s scheduled Nightly carried a `dispatch-release` job that ran `gh workflow run nightly.yml --ref releases/v0.3.0.beta` on every scheduled run, starting a second, independent Nightly with that branch's own workflow and source. This removes that job and the documentation that describes it.

## Changes

`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`

- Removes the `dispatch-release` job, including `RELEASE_REF: releases/v0.3.0.beta` and the `actions: write` permission it was the only job to request.
- Removes the header's statement that the scheduled build also dispatches an independent run for the release branch. The header now says the workflow is the scheduled build of the default branch, and that any other branch runs it only when dispatched by hand at that ref.

`.ci/README.md`, *Daily real-E2E prerequisites*

- The scheduled Daily covers `main` only. The paragraph no longer says each scheduled run dispatches a run at `releases/v0.3.0.beta`; it says a daily gate for another branch runs only when someone starts `Nightly` with `workflow_dispatch` at that ref, using that ref's own workflow and source.

Unchanged: `schedule` with `cron: "0 16 * * *"`, `workflow_dispatch`, and the `stamp`, `gate` (`profile: daily`, `secrets: inherit`) and `report` jobs. Manual `workflow_dispatch` at any ref is deliberately left available. Nothing on the release branch is modified; with no dispatch from `main` and no schedule of its own, it simply stops receiving scheduled runs.

## Verified diff

Checked on this branch, based on `main` at `90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed`:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `git grep` for `dispatch-release`, `RELEASE_REF`, `releases/v0.3.0.beta` | no matches anywhere in the repository |
| `git grep` for `gh workflow run` | one match, a generic example in `.agents/skills/ci/references/github.md` that dispatches `ci.yml` by hand; nothing dispatches to the release branch |
| Jobs in `nightly.yml` after the change | `stamp`, `gate`, `report` |
| Triggers | `schedule` (`cron: "0 16 * * *"`) and `workflow_dispatch` |
| `gate` | still `uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml` with `profile: daily` |
| README vs workflow | both state the schedule builds `main` only and that other refs run only by manual dispatch |
| `actionlint` on `nightly.yml` and `ci.yml` | clean |

The job being removed was added in a single earlier commit that touched only these two files, so nothing else depended on it, and no test or script reads `nightly.yml`.

244.body:
The `github` and `create-github-pr` skills both show `--head "$login:<branch>"` for opening a pull request. Under zsh, a letter right after that colon can be read as a modifier on `$login` (`:c`, `:h`, `:t`, `:r`, `:e`, and `:f` followed by one of them), so filling in the example for most branch names sends GitHub a head that is not the branch. GitHub answers with `No commits between …` and `Head ref must be a branch`, and the Troubleshooting entry for that message explained it only as a branch deleted after a merge. bash does not treat the colon specially, which is why the example looks correct.

## Changes

- Both examples now read `--head "${login}:<branch>"`, which bash and zsh expand the same way. `create-github-pr` keeps a one-line comment in the code block saying why the braces must stay.
- The `create-github-pr` Troubleshooting row for `No commits between` / `Head ref must be a branch` now gives both causes and how to tell them apart:
  - the branch was deleted when an earlier pull request from it merged — `git ls-remote <fork> 'refs/heads/<branch>'` is empty;
  - zsh mangled the head string — the branch exists, but the head echoed in the error no longer contains the whole branch name.
- The `github` skill has no Troubleshooting section, so it gets one sentence beside its example pointing to that row instead of a second copy that could drift.

Unchanged: placeholders such as `<login>:<branch>` and the gitcode skill's `<gitcode-login>:branch` are not shell expansions. No other skill puts an unbraced shell variable directly before a colon in a command.

## Validation

Each skill's `gh pr create` code block was executed verbatim in GNU bash 5.2.21 and zsh 5.9 (`zsh -f`), with `gh` and `git` stubbed so that `gh api user` returns `octocat` and `gh pr create` prints the `--head` it received. Only the angle-bracket placeholders were filled in. Nothing was sent to GitHub.

Before (the blocks as they are on `main`), identical for both skills:

| Branch | bash | zsh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chore/skill-zsh-head` | `octocat:chore/skill-zsh-head` | `octocathore/skill-zsh-head` |
| `fix/e2e-border` | `octocat:fix/e2e-border` | `octocat:fix/e2e-border` |
| `feat/release-notes` | `octocat:feat/release-notes` | `at/release-notes` |
| `release/v0.3.0` | `octocat:release/v0.3.0` | `octocatelease/v0.3.0` |
| `e2e/compact-process` | `octocat:e2e/compact-process` | `2e/compact-process` |

After: all 20 cases (2 skills × 2 shells × 5 branches) print `octocat:<branch>` with the branch intact.

`fix/` surviving is not a counterexample: `:f` only acts when the next letter is itself a modifier, and `i` is not. Which names break depends on the letters after the colon, so a spelling that worked for one branch proves nothing about the next — the Troubleshooting row says so.

247.author: zhaozhaozz
247.body:
When a finished model response carried a tool call whose arguments did not parse, the JiuwenSwarm model gateway rejected the whole turn. JiuwenSwarm never received the call, did not retry the model request, and the run or subagent failed, often after 20 to 40 minutes of completed research. The page then said "The model service rejected the request. Check the model configuration", although the provider had answered normally. On main Nightly [37875334064](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37875334064) this ended DRB-64 (main run, after 23 minutes) and twice killed the TC-E2E-01 delivery-signoff subagent, the first time after its MCP check had already returned `ok: true`. Fixes #236.

The failure was on the ScienceDiscovery side, before Swarm saw the call. JiuwenSwarm's pinned agent-core would have returned the parse error to the model as a tool result, and the native runtime already does (`INVALID_TOOL_ARGUMENTS`, `retryable: true`). Only finished responses on the Swarm path were fatal: truncated ones already went through bounded output-limit recovery.

## Withhold the response and let Swarm's recovery ask for the call again

`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts`: for a task turn that finished normally but has a call with `argsParseError`, the gateway now withholds every call of that response, appends `[invalid_tool_arguments:tool_calls_withheld]` with the tool names and parser messages, and finishes the response with `length`, exactly as it already finishes a cut response. Valid sibling calls are withheld too, so a response is either executed whole or not at all. V8 quotes an input excerpt in some `JSON.parse` messages (`Unexpected token 'c', ..."command": cat secret"... is not valid JSON`); that excerpt is removed, so no argument text reaches the notice. The private diagnostics file still records the full message.

`jiuwen_swarm/patches/workswarm0.2.6/0007-output-recovery.patch`: the existing per-instance recovery wrapper recognises the marker, classifies it as `invalid_tool_arguments`, and adds `[Tool argument recovery N/2; invalid_tool_arguments]` feedback that names the failing call and asks for one valid JSON object (escaping, smaller pieces for long text). It shares the existing budget of two extra model calls and raises the same structured `output_recovery_exhausted` error on exhaustion. The gateway reads the attempt back from that feedback; the two sides now point at each other where the `N/2` budget is shared.

Why withhold instead of returning an error: Swarm does not retry an error the gateway raises at the end of a response. By then the response is a 200 stream, so it arrives as an SSE `error` event, which neither the OpenAI SDK retries nor agent-core's recovery hooks (context overflow, stream stalls, tool-call loops) cover. Why not pass the call through to Swarm's own argument repair: the gateway re-serialises calls from parsed arguments (`toolCallsOf`), so the tool would run with `{}`; the adapter's platform-tool stream rewriter parses complete arguments at `finish_reason` and would end the stream; agent-core's bracket-balancing repair can turn an incomplete call into an executable one, which patch 0007 already avoids for cut responses; and the unparseable string would be replayed to the provider in later history. A withheld response is never replayed, so none of these layers see it.

## Only where every requester can recover

The recovery wrapper is installed on the run's own Swarm instance. With `SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_SUBAGENTS=jiuwenswarm`, Swarm's native sub-agents send model requests through the same gateway without it, and agent-core takes a `length` response without tool calls for a final answer: the sub-agent would have returned the notice as its result, and the parent's next request would clear the failure. In that mode the gateway keeps failing the request, as before. The default `task` mode runs every sub-agent as its own platform run with its own wrapper. Housekeeping calls (titles, compaction) also keep failing, since they have no wrapper.

## A run never ends silently on a withheld response

`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts`: if Swarm ends normally right after a withheld response, the run fails instead of completing. When recovery is exhausted, the error reads `Model returned invalid tool arguments (tools: run_shell) after 2 recovery attempts; gateway request chatcmpl-…`. The withheld-response notices (this one and the existing `[output_limit:tool_calls_withheld]`) are cut from the text shown to the user and from the run transcript; the adapter forwards every chat delta, so before this they appeared in the assistant's message.

## Name the failure instead of blaming the model configuration

`invalid-tool-call` is a new `RunFailureCode`. `classifyRunFailure` checks it first, because the tool names in the message are arbitrary and could contain words such as `transport`. The Web UI shows "The model wrote a tool call whose arguments could not be read, so it was not run and the run stopped. Retry the task; if it keeps happening, try another model." (and the Chinese equivalent) instead of the configuration hint.

## Let `setup` upgrade an install whose patches were revised in place

Patch 0007 is edited in place, as 0005 was in 94f98bbc; a separate patch on top would break the installer's idempotent re-apply. On a source install made before such an edit, `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup` used to stop with `output_recovery.py: already exists in working directory`, while `start` told the user to run setup. `scripts/swarm-patches.py apply` now compares the recorded patch set with the current one; when they differ in a source checkout, it first returns the patched paths to the pinned tag (removing files that patches created) and then applies the whole set. Wheel and site-packages targets are always built fresh and are unaffected.

## Validation

Local host with bubblewrap. ST and E2E ran on this head's tree (`fcbb8730`). UT ran while the head was `dbdd402d`, which differs only in `scripts/swarm-patches.py` resolving a relative `--patch-dir` and in the ST-only installer test.

| Layer | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| UT (`pnpm ci:ut`) | 3710 | 3710 | 3709 | 1 | 0 |
| ST (`pnpm ci:st`) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| E2E mocked (`pnpm ci:e2e`, profile `pr`) | 70 | 70 | 70 | 0 | 0 |

- The one local UT failure is `services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts` › "a blocked run holds its Session queue until the user decides permission" (`queued work did not overtake a blocked run in the same Session`, `2 !== 1`). It is pre-existing on this host: on unmodified `main` (`9189206d`), the same case run alone under `scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh` (as the layer runs it) fails with the same assertion. The GitHub Actions UT layer passed it on `ed849f6f` (3705/3705).
- ST includes the JiuwenSwarm SDK contract suite, 64 passed on a fresh `workswarm0.2.6` install with this branch's patches: `test_patch_installation.py` (clean install, idempotent re-apply, and the new upgrade of a checkout whose patches were revised in place, with a relative `--patch-dir`) and the three recovery tests (invalid-argument feedback, exhaustion with `"kind": "invalid_tool_arguments"`, the real ReAct loop executing only the re-issued call).
- Upgrade on a real install: in a clone of `workswarm0.2.6`, applying `main`'s patch set and then this branch's set through `scripts/swarm-patches.py apply` succeeds, `verify` passes and a second apply is a no-op. The same sequence with `main`'s installer stops with `output_recovery.py: already exists in working directory`.
- Unit tests: the gateway withholds every call of a finished response with unparseable arguments in streaming and unary modes (finish `length`, no `tool_calls`, marker with tool name and parser message); the notice carries no argument text even when V8's message quotes an excerpt; without a recovery boundary on every requester (`recoversWithheldCalls: false`) the request fails as before; recovery attempts are counted and a later successful task turn clears the failure; housekeeping still fails. The agent completes when the model re-issues the call; fails with `after 2 recovery attempts` when Swarm ends on a withheld response; keeps the old failure in `jiuwenswarm` sub-agent mode; and cuts both withheld notices from displayed text and the transcript. `classifyRunFailure` returns `invalid-tool-call`, also for a tool name containing `transport`, and every failure class has a zh-CN message.
- `pnpm typecheck` passes (UT layer `check:typecheck`).

GitHub Actions on `ed849f6f` (before the review follow-ups): UT 3705/3705, ST, E2E (mocked, JiuwenSwarm) 70/70, Coverage, Docker image and both binary releases succeeded. GitHub Actions run [37938879257](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37938879257) on `fcbb8730`: UT 3710/3710, ST, E2E (mocked, JiuwenSwarm) 70/70, Coverage, Docker image and both binary releases succeeded; the real daily E2E job is skipped on pull requests.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** on this head's tree, local isolated stack with the JiuwenSwarm backend and a scripted OpenAI-compatible model (`test/helpers/research-model.ts`). Real browser, real Swarm loop, real platform `run_shell` in the sandbox.

| Journey | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LR-01 invalid arguments are never executed and the model re-issues the call | The first response's `run_shell` has unterminated JSON. Nothing runs; the model's next request ends with `[Tool argument recovery 1/2; invalid_tool_arguments]` naming `run_shell`; the re-issued call runs and the run completes; the page never shows `tool_calls_withheld`. | PASS: exactly one shell execution (the re-issued call), none from the malformed one; three main-model requests; final answer shown; no notice on the page. |
| LR-17 repeated invalid arguments fail explicitly after bounded recovery | The same malformed call three times; recovery prompts 1/2 and 2/2; run `failed` with `invalid tool arguments (tools: run_shell) after 2 recovery attempts`; no shell execution; the page shows the new failure text and no notice. | PASS |
| LR-02 broken model stream does not execute a partial call | Unchanged: the run fails and nothing executes. | PASS |

The rest of the mocked slice also passed: research batch 20, standard batch 44 (plus the JiuwenSwarm checks: history, run-shell, host-tools, approvals, skills, trajectory, language all ok), literature batch 6.

Not covered: a real model. The trigger is non-deterministic model output (three occurrences in one Nightly, none reproducible on demand), so the evidence that DRB and TC-E2E-01 no longer end this way will come from the daily real E2E. The `jiuwenswarm` sub-agent mode is covered by unit tests only; no mocked journey runs that mode.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: A JiuwenSwarm research run, or one of its subagents, no longer ends when the model writes one tool call with malformed JSON arguments. The model is told which call failed and re-issues it; nothing from the malformed response is executed, and nothing of the internal notice is shown. If the model keeps failing, the run ends with a message that names the cause rather than the model configuration.
Compatibility and migration: A local JiuwenSwarm source install made before this change fails patch verification at `start` until `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup` is run once; setup now upgrades it in place. The Docker image, the binary release payload and the CI caches key on the patch files and rebuild on their own. API consumers see one more `errorCode` value, `invalid-tool-call`, on `run.failed`.

250.author: wyhohyw
250.body:
## Summary

- Reuse verified CAS object metadata and dependency edges during ref commits while continuing to walk the full reachable graph. New or changed objects still receive byte/hash and record-schema validation.
- Keep `validateClosure` as an explicit full audit. The commit cache is local to one `VersionStore` process and is published only after the whole closure succeeds.
- Reject objects that change during their first verification; add regressions for deleted, same-size corrupted, and mid-verification mutated dependencies. A cache-hit test also confirms that unchanged commits skip rereading while explicit audits do not.
- Update the existing English and Chinese CAS documentation with the commit fast path and its trust boundary.

Addresses #230.

## Evidence

Controlled local Biomni E2E pairs used the same direct DeepSeek API, `deepseek-flash`, no subagents, no Jina, and evaluation disabled. Model decisions and tool counts still varied, so the whole-run numbers are illustrative; the measured CAS stages are the direct performance signal.

| Case | Generation, baseline → optimized | `context_ref_commit` median | `step_commit` median |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DA-13-3 | 410.4 → 328.3 s | 989 → 151 ms | 1,345 → 256 ms |
| DA-14-1 | 1,007.5 → 815.5 s | 1,717 → 175 ms | 1,781 → 248 ms |

Both valid pairs passed and had zero child agents. They are one sample per case and do not establish a stable whole-run speedup percentage.

## Validation

- WSL `pnpm build`: passed.
- WSL `pnpm typecheck`: passed.
- WSL `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/cas test`: 28/28 passed after adding the cache-hit regression.
- WSL `pnpm docs:check`: passed.
- WSL Runner SEA binary tests: 33/33 passed after generating the required local SEA binary and running as the normal `sd-ci` user.
- WSL workspace tests excluding the Docker-dependent executor package: 1,074/1,075 API tests passed in a parallel run; the sole governed-download concurrency failure passed when its file was rerun separately (8/8). The trajectory recorder test passed 91/91 after using an isolated writable temp directory. Other workspaces reached by the recursive run passed.

`pnpm test` cannot complete in this local WSL environment because an unrelated executor integration test requires `docker`, which is not installed (`spawn docker ENOENT`). The previous PR head passed UT, ST, mocked E2E, both binary builds, Docker image, coverage, and CodeCheck. Checks for the latest head are running. Daily real E2E is skipped by workflow design.

## Review follow-ups

The main trajectory recorder owns a `VersionStore` for one run, while Runner also holds long-lived instances. Their cache grows with distinct committed objects until that instance ends; memory growth should be measured before choosing a limit that might reintroduce repeated hashing on long histories. The commit fast path intentionally rejects symlinks at object addresses through `lstat`; normal CAS publication creates regular files via hard links.

## Summary

- Reject an assistant turn with no non-whitespace answer and no tool call, even when the upstream reports `finish_reason=stop`. An explicit output-limit finish retains the existing recovery path.
- For OpenAI-compatible responses, retry one empty turn within the configured retry budget; then fail with bounded diagnostics that omit prompts, response text, tool arguments, and credentials. The per-run JiuwenSwarm model gateway enforces the same completion rule for alternate clients.
- Read SSE by event, including multiline `data:` records and a final line without a newline. Retain a useful terminal full-message snapshot without duplicating earlier deltas. Treat an upstream SSE error after partial output as a failure.
- Explain the completion rule in the existing English and Chinese Agent Backend documents.

Addresses the empty-turn and parsing portions of #245; endpoint latency comparisons remain open. Related to #246's stream-assembly diagnostics. #247 handles a separate invalid-tool-arguments recovery path and touches the model gateway, so its eventual merge may require a small rebase.
